science.title: Effects of deposition parameters and cobalt hexacyanocobaltate surface modification on magnetron-sputtered ZnIn₂S₄ thin film photoanodes
science.description: For the first time, ZnIn₂S₄ (ZIS) thin films were successfully prepared by magnetron sputtering and systematically investigated as photoanodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. The PEC performance of the layers strongly depended on the deposition parameters. The highest photocurrent density of 2.77 mA cm⁻² at 1.62 V vs. RHE was achieved for films deposited at 200 °C for 90 min, whereas films deposited at 300 °C for 90 min exhibited improved stability. The optimized ZIS photoanode was subsequently modified with a cobalt hexacyanocobaltate (Cohcc) surface layer formed via electrooxidation of a Co layer in an electrolyte containing Co(CN)₆³⁻. This surface modification improved photoanode performance, particularly in terms of stability, likely due to enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics at the electrode surface. Cohcc-modified photoanode generated almost 3 times higher photocurrent density after 100 s operation compared to unmodified photoanode. Electrochemical measurements performed under dark conditions further confirmed the role of Cohcc as cocatalyst toward OER. Overall, the results demonstrate that magnetron sputtering enables effective control over the properties of ZIS photoanodes through optimization of deposition parameters, while surface modification with cobalt hexacyanocobaltate represents a viable strategy for tuning interfacial kinetics and improving the functional performance of ZIS-based photoanodes.

science.title: Synthesis of a 2D/2D g-C3N4/UiO-66 S-scheme heterojunction for enhanced photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants
science.description: A unique 2D/2D g-C3N4/UiO-66 S-scheme nano-heterojunction was successfully developed via a straightforward hydrothermal approach to enhance the photocatalytic decomposition of organic contaminants under visible light. Comprehensive characterization techniques were employed to systematically examine the properties of the individual semiconductors and the newly synthesized heterostructure. PL, EIS and PR analyses confirmed that the photo-generated charge carries in 2D/2D nano-heterojunction/visible-light system have been efficiently separated. The improved photocatalytic performance could be ascribed to the strong contact between nanosheets of two semiconductors, uniform dispersion of UiO-66 nanosheets on the surface of large g-C3N4 nanosheets and synergistic effect of S-scheme electron-hole migration. The nano-heterojunction synthesized at the mass ratio of 0.2:1 of UiO-66 nanosheets to g-C3N4 nanosheets, g-C3N4/UiO-66/20, exhibited the highest MB photo-degradation rate (70.19% and 98.25% at catalyst dosages of 0.1 and 0.3 g/L, respectively), where the kinetic constant is 2.53 and 4.10 times of pristine g-C3N4 and UiO-66, respectively. Quenching experiments identified $$\:{.O}_{2}^{-}$$, $$\:.OH$$ and $$\:{h}^{+}$$ as the predominant active species, in descending order of importance. g-C3N4/UiO-66/20 nano-heterojunction indicated tremendous reusability and consistency, and it can be employed to successively uptake pollutant molecules from wastewater. This paper paves the way to construction of new visible-light driven 2D/2D nano-heterojunctions for the wastewater treatment process.

science.title: Physicists Find a Superconductor That 'Breaks' The Symmetry of Time - A First For Its Kind
science.description: Under certain conditions – such as bone-brittling temperatures lower than that of deep space – superconductors can conduct electricity without resistance and resultant energy loss.  Though they vary in their chemical composition, operational temperature ranges, and magnetic properties, superconductors come in two groupings.  First, conventional and unconventional superconductors differ in how their electrons become entangled in tandems called Cooper pairs, an identity-sharing state that allows them to gracefully glide through the atomic jumble of their materials to facilitate uninterrupted electric flow.  Secondly, type I and type II superconductors respond differently to magnetic fields, with distinct types of thresholds at which they abruptly stop operating as superconductors and start acting like regular conductors.  Unconventional and type II varieties are generally considered more exotic; the Lamborghinis of their domain, pushing physical boundaries because they require bespoke engineering.  They may also be more suited as workhorses used in technologies like MRIs, much as Lamborghinis used to be tractors.
